transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-01-20 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~54m
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendes (Helix Head of Platform), Anya Li (Helix SRE), Tom Becker (Helix CISO), Sofia Ruiz (Helix Director ML)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Post-incident handoff: discussed KV cache corruption hypothesis, blast-radius reduction tactics (circuit breakers, tight rate-limits, per-tenant pools), and mitigations for rollback / canary gating.
- Agreed on immediate patch for KV-cache eviction logic, smoke test plan, and timeline for sharing traces.
- Compliance questions about audit log retention and KMS key access during emergency rollback.

TOPICS:
1) Incident recap + suspected root cause
2) Immediate mitigations (circuit breaker, fallback routing)
3) Longer-term reliability changes (per-tenant warm pools, quota isolation)
4) Security & compliance gating for rollbacks
5) Next steps and owners

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Alright everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to make this a focused ops handoff after last week's outage. We'll run through the timeline, what we think happened, and then immediate containment and the medium term hardening items.
[00:18] Carlos (Helix): Cool. We're mainly here to make sure we can reduce the blast radius and not have the same ripple across payments. The board is... uh, they're uh, not thrilled, so we need a clear plan.
[00:29] Liam (Redwood SE): Yep. Quick note — apologies in advance for some of the noisy auto-transcript stuff, I will refer to the traces in the drive.
[00:36] Anya (Helix): And SLOs: our p50 is fine, p95/p99 spiked, so the user impact was intermittent but high-risk for some high-value tenants.
[00:47] Maya: Exactly. Quick timeline: 2026-01-14 02:03 UTC we saw first error increase; 02:30 we saw cascading retries that exhausted a Redis-like KV cache process on the Redwood side — this caused fallback to colder model variants and then queueing, amplifying latency.
[01:05] Tom (CISO): When you say KV cache, is that the prefix cache? We saw some anomalous keys in the audit.
[01:12] Liam: Yes — it's the prefix + KV layer that we use for hot-state. We suspect a race in our eviction path combined with a compaction GC on the node. In some cases the eviction didn't free the metadata, which then blocked new requests and caused retry storms.
[01:31] Sofia (ML): Just to be clear, did that cause model state corruption or just availability issues?
[01:36] Liam: Availability only — no weights changed. The KV entries are meta and prefix caches; the model binaries are untouched. But the availability meant some requests were routed to smaller models causing semantic drift.
[01:48] Carlos: We tracked a subset of customers who had 10x increased token costs because they hit fallback repeatedly. We need not only fix but also billing reconciliation.
[01:59] Priya (Redwood CSM): We'll coordinate billing remediation. Maya, we'll propose credits and a reconciliation spreadsheet.
[02:07] Maya: Yes. Action there. But operationally the immediate plan we discussed internally: 1) ship a hotfix to the eviction path to avoid leaked metadata 2) implement a temporary circuit breaker per-tenant to reject new requests when the KV node is above 85% mem 3) add a degraded but safe fallback route to a read-only replica with stricter token limits.
[02:32] Anya: How safe is the read-only replica approach? If we route to read-only it might serve stale prefixes — would that break some of our authorizations?
[02:42] Liam: It's safe for most prompt completions; not safe if you depend on latest tenant-specific state. We'll need to gate by customer config.
[02:49] Tom: From a compliance standpoint, we need an approval workflow for the degraded mode — can't just flip a switch for tenant A without an audit trail.
[02:56] Maya: Totally. We'll log the change and require an SSO-authorized approver. We can wire that into our Console audit events.
[03:05] [CROSSTALK]
[03:07] Carlos: Can you quantify the expected latency delta with the circuit breaker? Like what will P99 look like for the degraded route?
[03:14] Liam: For the read-only replica path, p99 is expected to be +40 to +90ms under load versus normal; the bigger win is preventing cascading retries which reduce tenant-wide tail.
[03:24] Sofia: Also concerned about quality regression when fallback to smaller models happens due to routing. We need to ensure quality monitoring alerts when semantic drift passes threshold.
[03:34] Maya: This is where Redwood Optimize recommendations can help — we'll run diffs on top-k completions for a small prompt suite. We'll tie regression alerts to a canary gate.
[03:44] Anya: Ok. What's the immediate timeline for hotfix?
[03:48] Liam: My team has a patch ready that fixes the eviction leak; we need to run it through our canary — suggests 2-day safety window: canary in prod for a low-traffic region, then wider rollout. So earliest deploy 2026-01-22, full roll 2026-01-24 if canary looks good.
[04:03] Carlos: Is there a fast-path we can take to stop the bleeding now — like disabling retries or ramping request throttling from Helix side?
[04:10] Anya: We can throttle client-side at our proxy but it's awkward for feature parity.
[04:14] Tom: We can toggle stricter rate-limits for the affected tenants, but we need coordination.
[04:19] Maya: We'll provide tenant-level circuit breaker configs; Helix can opt-in per tenant. We'll send recommended thresholds for each impacted tenant.
[04:27] [00:04:35] Priya: Note — we'll also create a 'safety net' playbook in the shared folder: step-by-step ops runbook to apply the circuit breaker and rollback instructions.
[04:40] Carlos: Great. On the longer term — you mentioned per-tenant warm pools?
[04:45] Liam: Right. The idea is isolate heavy tenants into dedicated warm pools so a single tenant cannot starve the global KV or GPU pools. This requires quota and scheduler changes; rough ETA 6–10 weeks.
[04:56] Sofia: That seems important. For us, the tenant who caused the problem was running a large batch rerank job off business hours which amplified the issue. If we had isolation they wouldn't have affected payments latency.
[05:11] Maya: We'll prioritize tenant isolation and per-tenant quotas in the next reliability sprint. We'll also add an emergency 'auto-mitigate' that triggers circuit-breaker based on cross-tenant error-rate heuristics.
[05:24] Anya: Rewrite of the eviction path — will that require all nodes restart? That worries us due to maintenance windows.
[05:31] Liam: The patch is rolling — no full cluster restart; it's safe to roll pod-by-pod. However some nodes might briefly reject requests during local upgrade. That's why we need canary gating.
[05:45] Tom: Audit-wise, we need immutable logs for any emergency changes. How do we ensure those are captured?
[05:51] Maya: Console will create an audit event and we'll make sure those events are forwarded to your SIEM. We'll also provide a signed manifest of who approved the change.
[06:03] Carlos: One area I want to emphasize — the billing refunds. We'll want line-item visibility per token and a precise reconciliation.
[06:10] Priya: We'll provide a runbook for billing reconciliation; but we'll need Helix to confirm which tenants to apply credits to.
[06:18] [00:06:22] Sofia: A non-technical ask — can we get a plain English postmortem doc for our execs? The board wants a timeline and mitigations separated into immediate / short / long.
[06:30] Maya: Yes — we'll generate a postmortem doc, include timelines, root cause, impact, mitigations, and the roadmap for hardening. We'll have a draft by 2026-01-23.
[06:41] Anya: Regarding repro — can Redwood provide a repro harness or synthetic that triggers similar eviction paths so we can run it internally?
[06:49] Liam: We'll include a repro harness in the shared drive. It won't match your exact traffic shape but it exercises the eviction/leak pattern. That will be part of the extra deliverable.
[06:58] Carlos: On the security front, the CISO wants confirmation that KMS keys are not accessible during emergency rollback and that key-rotation won't be impeded.
[07:07] Tom: Also want to know the retention for debug traces. If we need to do a forensics run, how long do you keep the detailed traces?
[07:14] Liam: By default we keep traces for 30 days. For this incident we can extend retention for Helix's namespace to 90 days temporarily.
[07:21] Tom: Good. Also need a timeline for SOC 2 relevant artifacts related to this change.
[07:26] Maya: We'll map the changes to control IDs and provide artifacts to help with your audit.
[07:31] [00:07:35] Carlos: One more question — did the auto-scaling behavior contribute? It looked like autoscaler added pods but they were unhealthy and made things worse.
[07:41] Liam: Autoscaler added pods due to perceived load; but the health checks were permissive. We're tightening the readiness probe to ensure only fully warmed pods receive traffic. Also added pre-warm hooks for the KV layer.
[07:56] Anya: What's the plan for warm-up? Are we going to keep ephemeral warm pools or maintain persistent warm instances for certain tenants?
[08:03] Liam: Both options on the table: persistent warm pools for a handful of enterprise tenants (reserved capacity) and ephemeral warm pools with accelerated warm-up for bursty tenants.
[08:12] Sofia: Persistent increase in cost is fine for us if it guarantees stability for payments.
[08:17] Maya: We'll draft a sizing estimate and expected costs for persistent warm pools per tenant.
[08:23] [00:08:25] Priya: Note — we'll send the quote and recommend configuration for Helix's top 10 tenants.
[08:30] Carlos: On the topic of model fallbacks — can Redwood flag responses that came from fallback models so we can detect semantic drift quicker?
[08:38] Liam: Yes, we can include metadata tokens indicating model variant. We'll also expose a regression metric that compares top-N completions to baseline.
[08:47] Sofia: That should help. We can automate a run that samples 1000 prompts/day and alert on scoring delta > threshold.
[08:54] Maya: We'll help set up that sampling and tie it to Redwood Optimize so alerts appear in Console.
[09:00] [00:09:02] Carlos: A nit — the transcript from previous postmortem had some typos; make sure the postmortem doc is clean.
[09:08] Maya: Noted. We'll produce a polished doc.
[09:12] Anya: For the canary gating metrics, propose we use these three: 1) p99 latency not worse than +50ms, 2) error-rate delta < 0.1%, 3) regression score delta < 0.02 across prompt suite.
[09:26] Liam: Sounds reasonable. We'll provide dashboards and configure alerts.
[09:30] Tom: For the emergency rollback window, what's the expected RTO if we need to roll back the patch?
[09:36] Liam: Rollback is pod-by-pod; RTO is about 12–15 minutes for a complete rollback assuming no dependency lock. We'll document the exact steps.
[09:45] Carlos: Fine. On shared artifacts — where will we put the traces and the repro?
[09:49] Maya: Shared drive link (internal): https://redwood.share/helix/incident-2026-01 (note: placeholder in transcript) — includes traces, repro harness, canary dashboards, and the postmortem draft.
[09:59] [00:10:00] Priya: I'll also attach a billing reconciliation template and the credits proposal.
[10:04] Anya: One remaining risk — if the eviction leak is only partially mitigated we could still see recurring small blips. Do you have a plan for ongoing monitoring and regression detection?
[10:14] Liam: Yes, telemetry: we'll add a KV-metadata-leak metric that counts leaked entries per node, plus alerting if leak-rate > threshold for 10 min. We'll also add a weekly health check report for the next quarter.
[10:29] Sofia: Will that metric be in our Console or in our Grafana?
[10:33] Maya: We'll surface it in Console and push a Grafana dashboard to your infra team.
[10:39] [00:10:44] Tom: A final compliance question — emergency fixes that change data handling need to be vetted for PII handling. Does the eviction patch alter any retention behavior?
[10:52] Liam: No, the patch only touches metadata bookkeeping and eviction logic; nothing changes retention or encryption flows. We'll include a short security note to confirm.
[11:01] Carlos: Excellent. Let's run through explicit next steps and owners.
[11:05] Maya: Summarizing: 1) Maya/Liam — upload traces + repro + KV patch (2026-01-22) 2) Helix (Anya) — run smoke tests and report (2026-01-25) 3) Priya — billing reconciliation + credits proposal (2026-01-23) 4) Tom — confirm compliance gating (2026-01-24).
[11:25] Anya: One more ask: can Redwood provide a simulation of worst-case retry amplification so we can justify warm-pool costs?
[11:31] Liam: We'll include synthetic load shapes in the repro. It will show amplification when retries are enabled vs disabled.
[11:36] Carlos: Ok. Anything else on the call?
[11:40] Priya: I'll schedule the follow-up check-in on 2026-01-27 to review canary results and smoke tests.
[11:46] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the postmortem draft and shared artifacts.
[11:51] [00:11:52] END OF CALL NOTES: Action items repeated in notes and uploaded.
